newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Chirac arrives in Hungary for two-day state visit.
newsitem.headline: Chirac arrives in Hungary for two-day state visit.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac arrived in Budapest on Thursday to begin a two-day state visit, the first by a French head of state since the end of communism in Hungary.
Chirac was is expected to tell his hosts in a speech to a gathering of dignataries at Budapest's parliament that France hopes Hungary will join the European Union in 2000.

European Commission experts have described such a deadline as unrealistic, saying it would probably take at least more two years for the first former communist Central European states seeking admission to join.

A dozen top industrialists were accompanying Chirac, including the chairmen of state electricity and gas companies EDF and GDF, missiles and electronics firm Matra, construction giant Bouygues and utilities company Lyonnaise des Eaux.
The other major issue in talks with President Arpad Gonzc and Prime Minister Gyula Horn will be Hungary's bid for NATO membership, which France says it supports unreservedly.

Chirac will also decorate a dozen Hungarians with French connections who distinguished themselves in the 1956 anti-Stalinist uprising and will address a 2,000-strong gathering of French-speaking Hungarian youth.
Chirac's predecessor, Francois Mitterrand, visited Budapest just months before Hungary held its first democratic elections in 1990.
